question: Does the 27-cell v2 family survive multiplicity correction, and does the bidirectionality claim in sec 5.3 survive?
computed_by: MAIN, independently, from sections/tab_v2_full.tex as the sole input
method: tie-aware Benjamini-Hochberg step-up q-values: q_(i) = min_{j>=i} m*p_(j)/j, enforced monotone; Bonferroni at alpha/m

VERDICT_ON_THE_DISPUTE.there_was_no_dispute: My pre-compaction note framed R-claude-stats V13 and the meta-review 3.7 as reaching OPPOSITE conclusions on the same 27 numbers. That was MY error, not theirs. Both say BH rejects 6 and that olmo2/keep14 is RETAINED. I had read 'retained' as 'the finding is retained'; in multiple testing it means the NULL is retained, i.e. the cell FAILS correction. The two reviewers agree exactly, and my arithmetic reproduces both.

CORRECTION_TO_BOTH_REVIEWERS.severity: precision defect that would have propagated into the paper had I copied their wording
CORRECTION_TO_BOTH_REVIEWERS.R-claude-stats_wrote: 'The 27-cell v2 re-analysis receives no multiplicity correction, and neither \'trace signal\' cell survives one over the paper\'s own tabulated family.'
CORRECTION_TO_BOTH_REVIEWERS.meta_review_wrote: 'Bonferroni (alpha/27 = 0.001852) rejects only the 5 anchors, so both \'trace signal\' cells fail.'
CORRECTION_TO_BOTH_REVIEWERS.why_wrong: Under BH at q=0.05, Qwen3/k14 DOES survive (rank 6, p=0.0066 <= 6*0.05/27 = 0.011111, q_BH = 0.029700). Only under Bonferroni do both fail. Each reviewer's own step-by-step enumeration states that rank 6 rejects, so each contradicts its own summary sentence.
CORRECTION_TO_BOTH_REVIEWERS.consequence_if_uncorrected: Writing 'neither trace-signal cell survives correction' into the paper would be FALSE for BH, i.e. it would understate the paper's own surviving evidence -- an error against the authors, but an error.
CORRECTION_TO_BOTH_REVIEWERS.what_is_actually_true: BH over the 27-cell family retains ONE of the two trace-signal cells (Qwen3/k14) and drops the other (OLMo-2/keep14). Since OLMo-2/keep14 is the ONLY cell moving in the upward direction, the surviving half of the bidirectionality claim is the downgrade only.

IMPLICATION_FOR_SEC_5_3.current_sentence: 'It withdraws the published above-floor capability label for qwen3/k14, replacing it with TRACE_SIGNAL, while olmo2/keep14 moves from at-floor to TRACE_SIGNAL. Re-sorting in both directions is evidence that the criterion is doing more than shrinking effects.'
IMPLICATION_FOR_SEC_5_3.defect: The upward direction is carried by exactly one cell whose q_BH = 0.0663. Under correction over the family the table itself defines (one table, one null, one statistic, one item set), the read-out re-sorts in ONE direction only, so 'doing more than shrinking effects' has no BH-surviving support.
IMPLICATION_FOR_SEC_5_3.downgrade_direction_survives: qwen3/k14's v2 p=0.0066 has q_BH=0.0297, so the withdrawal of its above-floor label IS supported after correction.
IMPLICATION_FOR_SEC_5_3.required_fix: Report q_BH per cell; state the bidirectionality as an uncorrected per-cell observation; rest no conclusion on it.

SCOPE_LIMIT_STATED_HONESTLY: BH assumes p-values that are independent or positively-regression-dependent. These 27 cells share the MMLU-Pro item axis and nest arms within families, so PRDS is plausible but unverified here. This computation shows what the paper's own stated correction yields on its own tabulated family; it does not establish that BH is the right correction for this dependence structure. The paper's existing objection to off-the-shelf correction (Appendix app:designated) still applies -- but it cannot be used to avoid reporting the number, because the paper already applies BH to its 12-cell comparison.
